facts.statement: Duriavenator fossils date to the Bajocian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Bajocian

facts.statement: Upper and lower jaw bones were collected near Sherborne in Dorset in 1882.
facts.quote: In 1882, upper and lower jaw bones of a dinosaur were collected near Sherborne in Dorset

facts.statement: The specimen was recognized as a different species by 1964 and described as Megalosaurus hesperis in 1974.
facts.quote: By 1964, the specimen was recognised as belonging to a different species, and in 1974 it was described as a new species of Megalosaurus, M. hesperis

facts.statement: Roger B. J. Benson moved the species to its own genus, Duriavenator, in 2008.
facts.quote: Roger B. J. Benson moved M. hesperis to its own genus in 2008, Duriavenator

facts.statement: Duriavenator is estimated to have been 5 to 7 meters long and weighed 1 ton.
facts.quote: Estimated to have been 5-7 m long and weighed 1 t, Duriavenator has been described as a medium-sized theropod.

facts.statement: Duriavenator had about four teeth in the premaxilla, 14 to 16 in the maxilla, and 14 to 15 in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: It had about four teeth in the premaxilla, about 14–16 in the maxilla behind, and about 14–15 in the dentary of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Duriavenator is known from the Upper Inferior Oolite Formation, which is of Bajocian age.
facts.quote: Duriavenator is known from the Upper Inferior Oolite Formation which is Bajocian in age, a stage in the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses from 2010 onwards show Duriavenator belongs to the family Megalosauridae and is among the oldest tetanuran theropods.
facts.quote: phylogenetic analyses in 2010 and onwards have shown it to be among the oldest tetanuran theropods (a diverse group that includes modern birds), and to belong in the family Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: Edward Cleminshaw obtained skull bones and teeth from the Inferior Oolite in Greenhill near Sherborne in Dorset in 1882.
facts.quote: In 1882, the British scientist and businessman Edward Cleminshaw obtained skull bones and teeth of a dinosaur from the freestone of the Inferior Oolite in Greenhill near Sherborne in Dorset, England.

facts.statement: Richard Owen considered the fossils to belong to Megalosaurus bucklandii in 1883.
facts.quote: In 1883, Owen considered these fossils to have belonged to the species Megalosaurus bucklandii

facts.statement: Michael Waldman prepared the specimen in 1964–1965 and designated it the holotype for Megalosaurus hesperis in 1974.
facts.quote: Michael Waldman further prepared the specimen in 1964–1965 and made it the holotype (on which the scientific name is based) of a new species of Megalosaurus, M. hesperis in 1974.

facts.statement: In 2008, Roger B. J. Benson redescribed the holotype, identified distinguishing features, and moved the species to the genus Duriavenator.
facts.quote: In 2008, Benson redescribed the 'M.' hesperis holotype (aided by casts of the block made prior to preparation) and identified several features distinguishing it from Megalosaurus and other related theropods, and moved it to its own genus, Duriavenator, creating the new combination D. hesperis.

facts.statement: The palatal process on the Duriavenator premaxilla was more prominent than in other basal tetanurans.
facts.quote: The lowest of these is the palatal process, which was prominent in Duriavenator compared to other basal (early diverging) tetanurans

facts.statement: The Duriavenator maxilla features eleven foramina approximately 2 mm in diameter on the surface connecting with the premaxilla.
facts.quote: There are eleven foramina about 2 mm in diameter each as well as smaller foramina present on the lower part of this surface

facts.statement: Two pneumatic chambers are visible in the corner of the antorbital fossa of the Duriavenator maxilla.
facts.quote: Two pneumatic (air-filled) chambers can be seen through a break in the maxilla in a corner of the antorbital fossa

facts.statement: All 11 tooth sockets in the Duriavenator maxilla contained emerging or fully-erupted teeth.
facts.quote: All 11 tooth sockets of the maxilla contain emerging or fully-erupted teeth

facts.statement: The frontmost tooth crowns of Duriavenator have 8 to 9 serrations per 5 mm on their front and hind edges.
facts.quote: There are 8–9 serrations per 5 mm on the front and hind edges at the mid-height of the frontmost tooth crowns

facts.statement: The interdental plates in the Duriavenator maxilla are roughly pentagonal, unfused, and extend to the bottom of the side wall.
facts.quote: The interdental plates are roughly pentagonal and unfused, and extend to the bottom level of the side wall of the maxilla

facts.statement: The Duriavenator dentary features tall, roughly pentagonal interdental plates on the inner side of the tooth row.
facts.quote: The dentary of the lower jaw has tall, roughly pentagonal interdental plates on the inwards side of the tooth row

facts.statement: Two roughly oval Meckelian foramina are located in succession near the front end of the Meckelian groove in the Duriavenator dentary.
facts.quote: There are two Meckelian foramina in succession close to the front end of the groove, both with roughly oval outlines

facts.statement: The preserved right dentary of the Duriavenator holotype contains parts of only the first 13 tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The right dentary only preserves parts of the first 13 tooth sockets

facts.statement: The first three tooth sockets in the Duriavenator dentary are roughly circular, with the third being the largest.
facts.quote: The first three tooth sockets are roughly circular, and the third is the largest of them all

facts.statement: Waldman suggested Duriavenator may have had five premaxillary tooth sockets, which would make it unique among megalosauroids, though this number cannot be directly observed in the specimen.
facts.quote: Waldman suggested there were five tooth sockets in the premaxilla, and if this is true, Duriavenator would have been unique among megalosauroids, which have either lower or higher numbers of premaxillary teeth

facts.statement: The Duriavenator holotype preserves tooth sockets in only two locations: two in the left premaxilla and none in the right premaxilla.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen only preserves two tooth sockets in the left premaxilla (the right premaxilla does not preserve any)

facts.statement: The species was originally classified under a different genus until it was moved to its own genus, Duriavenator, in 2008.
facts.quote: Until it was re-described and moved to its own genus Duriavenator in 2008, the higher level classification of the species was unclear

facts.statement: In 2008, researchers confirmed that Duriavenator belongs to the group Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Benson stated in 2008 that it was important to confirm the tetanuran status of early members of the group, such as Duriavenator

facts.statement: The genus Duriavenator was established by Benson in 2008.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Benson, 2008

facts.statement: The species D. hesperis was originally described by Waldman in 1974.
facts.quote: species_authority: Waldman, 1974

facts.statement: Duriavenator lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately between 171 and 167 million years ago, in the Bajocian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 171 a 167 millones de años, durante el Bajociense

facts.statement: During the Middle Jurassic, Britain was located in the subtropics and formed part of an island archipelago.
facts.quote: During the Middle Jurassic, Britain was located in the subtropics, and along with the rest of Western Europe formed a part of an island archipelago

facts.statement: In 2009, researchers noted that the front teeth of Duriavenator were longer than the back teeth, circular in cross-section, and inclined forwards.
facts.quote: Benson and Barrett pointed out in 2009 that the teeth at the front of the dentary in Duriavenator were longer than those at the back, were circular in cross-section, and were slightly inclined forwards

facts.statement: In 2016, Paul suggested that megalosaurids like Duriavenator were ambush predators that preyed on sauropods and stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Paul suggested in 2016 that megalosaurids were ambush predators, whose prey included sauropods and stegosaurs

facts.statement: In 2017, Rothschild and Naples hypothesized that lateral grooves on Duriavenator's dentary were sensory organs analogous to fish lateral lines.
facts.quote: The American palaeontologists Bruce M. Rothschild and Virginia Naples suggested in 2017 that the lateral grooves on the dentary of Duriavenator were similar to those of albertosaurine tyrannosaurids, interpreting these grooves as sensory organs analogous to the lateral lines of fish

facts.statement: The genus name Duriavenator combines the Latin words for Dorset and hunter.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina los vocablos en latín del antiguo nombre de Dorset, Duria, con venator que significa cazador

facts.statement: Early estimates suggested Duriavenator was a medium-to-large hunter about 9 meters long.
facts.quote: Duriavenator era un cazador de tamaño mediano a grande que, según las antiguas estimaciones, tenía unos 9 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Roger Benson estimated the animal was at least one-third shorter, about 5 meters long.
facts.quote: según Benson era al menos un tercio más corto, unos 5 metros.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that it was 7 meters long and weighed 1 ton.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul lo sostuvo en 2010 a 7 metros, con un peso de 1 tonelada.

facts.statement: The known skull fragment measures approximately 40 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El fragmento del cráneo mide aproximadamente 40 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The premaxilla held 4 teeth while the maxilla held at least 13.
facts.quote: El premaxilar porta 4 dientes, mientras que el maxilar posee al menos 13.

facts.statement: The longest maxillary tooth had a root measuring 13 centimeters.
facts.quote: El tercer diente maxilar más largo tiene una raíz de 13 centímetros.

facts.statement: In 1974, Michael Waldman named the fossil, found during construction in 1882 by Edward Cleminshaw near Sherborne, as the new species Megalosaurus hesperis.
facts.quote: En 1974 Michael Waldman nombró un fósil encontrado en un proyecto de construcción en la primavera de 1882 por el contratista Edward Cleminshaw en piedras de una cantera en Green Hill, cerca de Sherborne, como una nueva especie del género Megalosaurus, Megalosaurio hesperis.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil BNMH R. 332 was found in the upper layer of the Lower Oolite dating to the late Bajocian, around 168 million years ago.
facts.quote: El fósil, holotipo BNMH R. 332, fue encontrado en una capa, llamada capa superior del Oolito Inferior que data de finales del Bajociano, alrededor de 168 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: In 2008, Roger Benson erected the new genus Duriavenator based on his cladistic analysis of Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: En 2008 Roger Benson dio, según su más reciente y completo análisis cladístico de Megalosauridae, su propio género al fósil Duriavenator

facts.statement: Shared unique characteristics indicate Duriavenator was a member of the clade Tetanurae and specifically the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Los sinapomorfias características que son únicas a un grupo de parentesco particular, compartidos, indican que Duriavenator era un miembro del clado Tetanurae y más específicamente de la familia Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: According to Benson, Duriavenator is one of the oldest known species that certainly belongs to the Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Según Benson, Duriavenator es también una de las especies más antiguas conocidas, de la cual es muy cierto que pertenecen a los Tetanurae.

facts.statement: A 2012 analysis by Matthew Carrano found Duriavenator to be a basal member of Megalosaurinae.
facts.quote: Un análisis de Matthew Carrano de 2012 encontró a Duriavenator como un miembro basal de Megalosaurinae.

facts.statement: Duriavenator lived during the Bajocian stage, between 168.6 and 168.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (168.6 to 168.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The species name 'hesperis' refers to Hesperia, which British authors associated with Great Britain or West Dorset.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, "occidental" en latín, se refiere a Hesperia, la mitología griega de la Isla de la Bendición occidental, que a los británicos les gustaba identificar con Gran Bretaña, pero también a West Dorset.
